reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the resource-review contract, resource rubric, fresh-review framework, Linkage resource-review context, Linkage StructureDefinition report, the deterministic aggregate, direct SearchParameters and HttpRestBehavior findings for Linkage, and the R4/R6 package evidence for Linkage. Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were treated as context only because the assessed resource is Linkage, not Resource or DomainResource.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 Linkage was trial-use/FMM 0, so the compatibility burden is weak compared with mature or normative resources. That softens the case for retaining the whole resource, but it does not erase migration risk where Linkage captured record-equivalence, source-of-truth, alternate, or historical-record semantics.

overall.oneLineConclusion: R6 removes the Linkage resource, so R4 Linkage instances need a migration/disposition program; preserving the small legacy role terminology remains a low-cost standards concern.

reasoning.thesisMd: The resource-level break is not a local element rename or binding tweak: R4 defines concrete `Linkage` instances, while the supplied R6 package has no `StructureDefinition-Linkage.json` and no package-index entry for Linkage. An R6-only validator, parser, generated model, REST route inventory, and search surface therefore have no standard resource to accept. Because R4 maturity was FMM 0/trial-use, retaining the whole arbitrary-resource linkage model is not strongly compelled, but systems that used it still need deliberate migration policy.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: Migration is a removed-resource disposition. R4 Linkage carried `active`, `author`, and repeating `item` entries, with each item assigning a required role and referencing any FHIR Resource. There is no standard same-resource R6 destination for that bundle of semantics. Some patient identity use cases may have resource-specific patterns such as patient links, but those do not preserve the general arbitrary-resource set, author, active status, or `source`/`alternate`/`historical` role semantics. Implementers must choose archival retention, local extension/profile support, or case-by-case mapping.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: The resource identity removal makes a resource-level migration program unavoidable before old element names or search parameters can help much. Endpoint aliases or retaining Linkage search parameters would effectively require retaining an obsolete Linkage resource surface, which is not obviously low-cost for an FMM 0 model. The important exception is the LinkageType terminology: preserving the small canonical CodeSystem/ValueSet as retired or historical would reduce migration ambiguity without reintroducing the resource.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: Keeping Linkage itself as a deprecated R6 resource would be the broadest less-breaking option, but it carries generated-model, validation, endpoint, and search-surface cost for a low-maturity arbitrary-resource linkage model. Retaining only `http://hl7.org/fhir/linkage-type` and its value set is much narrower: it preserves the meaning of legacy role codes for migration tools, extensions, and archival validation while avoiding support for active R6 Linkage instances.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: The direct behavior findings matter because they are the operational face of the same removal. The base CapabilityStatement no longer advertises removed-resource endpoints including Linkage, and Linkage-only R4 search parameters such as `author`, `item`, and `source` disappear because their base resource is gone. These are real runtime/API breaks, but for Linkage they are downstream of the accepted resource-removal decision rather than independent reasons to preserve the full resource.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: The deterministic aggregate concluded `majorMigrationAlreadyUnavoidable=Yes`, `removed-or-replaced-resource`, and `migration-program-dominates`. I agree with that resource-level posture after independently checking the resource absence, content model, direct behavior impacts, and low R4 maturity. The aggregate should still not be read as dismissing the terminology Revisit finding; that low-cost preservation issue remains standards-review-worthy.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: The supplied inputs did not include official R6 narrative pages, Jira rationale, or a final published R6 package. The package evidence is strong that Linkage is absent from R6 ballot4 core, but non-core implementation-guide migration guidance or final R6 changes could refine the recommended disposition.

findingConsiderations.title: Linkage resource is absent from the R6 core package
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the decisive resource-level break. R4 has a concrete `Linkage` resource, while the R6 package/index has no same-name StructureDefinition, so old instances and generated resource APIs have no standard R6 target. FMM 0 makes the removal more proportionate, but not optional for migration planning.

findingConsiderations.title: R4 Linkage content model has no standard R6 destination
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This shows why migration is more than changing `resourceType`. Linkage combined active status, author attribution, arbitrary-resource item references, and role semantics. Without a standard R6 destination, implementers need business policy to decide whether to archive, extend, or map each linkage assertion.

findingConsiderations.title: Linkage item role terminology is not present in the R6 core package
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the main avoidable issue left after accepting resource removal. Retaining the small `source`/`alternate`/`historical` CodeSystem and ValueSet as retired or historical would be much cheaper than preserving the whole resource and would help migration tools avoid losing source-of-truth semantics.

findingConsiderations.title: The full base CapabilityStatement no longer advertises many R4 resource REST endpoints
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Linkage is one of the removed endpoint surfaces. This matters for generic clients and conformance tooling that build route inventories from the base CapabilityStatement, but for Linkage the endpoint loss is derivative of the resource removal rather than a separate low-cost compatibility target.

findingConsiderations.title: Search parameters whose only R4 bases were removed resources disappear from the R6 search surface
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: R4 Linkage search parameters such as `author`, `item`, and `source` disappear with the resource. That is a concrete API migration chore for clients that queried Linkage, but preserving those searches in R6 would require a legacy Linkage endpoint or explicit server-specific compatibility support.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 invocation matrix changes instance-level Resource $validate request semantics
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Shared Resource behavior can affect generic tooling, but it was not scored for Linkage because Linkage is not Resource or DomainResource. It does not change the Linkage-specific conclusion, which is already dominated by removal from R6 core.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Publish explicit Linkage migration/disposition guidance: confirm removal from R6 core, state whether any endorsed successor pattern exists, and distinguish archival retention, local extension/profile support, and resource-specific mappings such as patient-link workflows.

Revisit the disappearance of the LinkageType CodeSystem and ValueSet. Prefer retaining the canonical `source`, `alternate`, and `historical` terminology as retired or historical migration terminology even if the Linkage resource remains removed.

Document the REST/search consequences for implementers: R6 core has no Linkage endpoint and no Linkage-only `author`, `item`, or `source` search surface, so servers offering legacy support should advertise it explicitly outside the core expectation.

caveats: The supplied R6 package is ballot4 and marked not for publication; final R6 content may differ.
Official diff text, Jira rationale, and narrative migration pages were not available in the local inputs.
Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were considered only as context and not as Linkage-specific break drivers.
